area: F7 package integrity: gates, documentation claims, measured numbers, test-suite integrity, layering (cycle B, slot F7)

findings.title: Twelve MIPLIB corpus cases pass silently in every debug build, including CI's test job and its Thread Sanitizer job
findings.claim: HANDBOOK Testing: 'tests that need a missing instance report a known issue instead of failing', 'A debug build runs a reduced corpus'; .github/workflows/ci.yml:50 'Rule C10: Thread Sanitizer is clean on the integration suite'; README §5 'Thread Sanitizer: No reports on the ... branch-and-bound, CP-SAT, ... integration and liveness targets'; CorpusTests.swift:144-148 'CP-SAT as it runs by default ... proves every pure-integer instance of the set optimal'.
findings.observed: CorpusTests.swift:125/151/171 'guard !Self.slow.contains(instance.name) || Slow.enabled else { return }', and Slow.enabled is false in any DEBUG build without ZTRONLP_SLOW_TESTS=1 (CorpusTests.swift:9-17). 12 of the 23 MIPLIB parameter cases (BranchAndBound with both node engines on stein45/lseu/enigma/mod008; CPSAT() on stein45/lseu/mod008/p0201; CPSAT(lpPropagator:false) on stein45/lseu/enigma/mod008) return before solving and are reported as passed, with no skip and no known issue. In debug, cpSatWithoutTheLPPropagator reports '6 test cases passed after 4.107 seconds' with no known issue, because its mod008 case returns before solving. In release the same case runs into its 60 s limit and records the known issue (75.9 s). Baseline TSAN, also a debug build: 66.5 s, no known issue. CI's build-and-test job ('swift test') and its thread-sanitizer job are debug builds without ZTRONLP_SLOW_TESTS. Only the release 'corpora' job runs the twelve cases. So TSAN never runs the largest parallel searches: stein45 B&B (55k nodes), lseu and enigma B&B, and CP-SAT on stein45, lseu, mod008 and p0201. The smaller parallel searches (p0033, stein27, flugpl, egout, misc03 and p0201 B&B) still run under TSAN.
findings.whyWrong: A case that runs nothing is counted as a pass, and it is among the 546 that README §5 reports as passed. The package itself uses .enabled(if:) (SATTests) and withKnownIssue (missing corpus) to make such gaps visible. Correctness is still covered by CI's release corpora job. The race check is not: the TSAN gate covers less than README §5's TSAN row and ci.yml's 'clean on the integration suite' suggest, and it leaves out the longest multi-worker searches.
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer && swift test --filter 'MIPLIBCorpusTests/cpSatWithoutTheLPPropagator'  (passes in ~4 s, no known issue; log verification/cycle-B/F7-debug-cpsat-nolp.log)  vs  swift test -c release --filter 'MIPLIBCorpusTests/cpSatWithoutTheLPPropagator'  (~76 s, records the mod008 known issue). Baseline: grep -n 'Test cpSatWithoutTheLPPropagator\|known issue' verification/baseline/03-test-debug.log verification/baseline/04-test-release-integration-liveness.log verification/baseline/05-tsan.log
findings.evidence: debug: '✔ Test cpSatWithoutTheLPPropagator(_:) with 6 test cases passed after 4.107 seconds.' (no known issue); release baseline: '━ Test cpSatWithoutTheLPPropagator(_:) with 6 test cases passed after 75.888 seconds with 1 known issue.' ('mod008: .feasible(stoppedBy: timeLimit), incumbent 333.0 vs 307.0'); TSAN baseline: '✔ Test cpSatWithoutTheLPPropagator(_:) with 6 test cases passed after 66.481 seconds.' (no known issue)
findings.documented: Partly: HANDBOOK Testing says a debug build runs a reduced corpus and that ZTRONLP_SLOW_TESTS=1 adds the slow MIPLIB instances. It does not say the omitted cases report as passed, nor that the TSAN job (debug) excludes them; README §5's TSAN row does not mention it.

findings.title: Scripts/lint.sh enforces less than rules C3 and C6 (and C2) state; C3 and C6 never scan Tests/
findings.claim: Scripts/lint.sh:5-8 ('C3 every @unchecked Sendable is listed and must carry an // INVARIANT: comment', 'C6 no DispatchSemaphore, Thread.sleep, blocking command-buffer wait or DispatchGroup wait', 'C2 no global mutable variables'); HANDBOOK Testing ('every @unchecked Sendable listed with its invariant, no blocking primitives'); SPECIFICATION-v0.2 §2.2 ('no new @unchecked Sendable (the count stays at one); Scripts/lint.sh must hold after every package').
findings.observed: On a synthetic tree with one violation per file, lint flags only 'var plainGlobal = 0', 'static var a = 0' and an @unchecked Sendable without an INVARIANT comment (rc=1, 3 hits). It lets through: '@unchecked' and 'Sendable' on separate lines (not even counted, so the count of one is not enforced); an @unchecked Sendable whose only '// INVARIANT:' belongs to a neighbouring declaration within 8 lines; MTLCommandBuffer.waitUntilScheduled() (a blocking command-buffer wait); DispatchQueue.global().sync {}; NSLock; NSCondition.wait(); Darwin.sleep(1); 'public private(set) var'; an indented file-scope var inside #if; 'static var b : Int = 0'; a static var initialised on the next line; and a Tests/ file with @unchecked Sendable, Thread.sleep and DispatchSemaphore.
findings.whyWrong: The checks are line-based greps for fixed spellings, and C3/C6 scan Sources only. Swift 6 mode rejects the C2 cases at compile time, but it does not reject blocking calls or a hidden @unchecked Sendable, so for C3 and C6 the lint is the only gate. The gap is latent: none of these constructs is in the tree today.
findings.repro: bash /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/cycle-B/F7-lint/Scripts/lint.sh   (a verbatim copy of Scripts/lint.sh; its ROOT is verification/cycle-B/F7-lint, whose Sources/T/*.swift and Tests/TT/*.swift hold one case each)
findings.evidence: Output lists only Sources/T/c2_plain.swift:1, Sources/T/c2_static.swift:1, the C3 entries c3_borrowed_invariant.swift:3 (accepted) and c3_noinvariant.swift:1 (flagged), '2 in total'; c3_split.swift, c6_*.swift, c2_privateset/indented/static_spacecolon/static_multiline.swift and Tests/TT/tests_violations.swift produce no output.

findings.title: README §5 Hilbert table: the 'Answers with a warning' column is wrong at orders 4 and 5
findings.claim: README.md:615-616 (Linear programs: ill-conditioned ones): order 4 '0 of 12', order 5 '3 of 12'; 'The warnings at orders 5 and 6 are the interior point's, whose normal equations stall there'; 'Measured with the engines as they are now.'
findings.observed: 4 of 12 at order 4 and 4 of 12 at order 5. InteriorPoint() attaches 'N column(s) have more than 30% nonzeros; the normal equations will be dense (§8.3)' to every Hilbert answer from order 4 on, and at order 5 the stall warning is on 3 of the 4 forms. Every other cell of the table matches what I measured (condition estimate, dense-solve error, per-engine distance, worst objective error, all 120 solves optimal).
findings.whyWrong: The count is deterministic and differs from the table. The dense-column warning is the one README §4 Limits documents ('a warning says so').
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-B && swift build --product F7 && .build/debug/F7 hilbert ; .build/debug/F7 hilbertwarn 4 5 6   (Slots/F7/Hilbert.swift)
findings.evidence: '4 2.84e+04 5.30e-13 5.30e-13 6.12e-13 5.30e-13 3.50e-16 4/12 optimalx12'; '5 9.44e+05 5.77e-12 5.84e-12 8.21e-12 5.77e-12 1.38e-16 4/12 optimalx12'; 'order 4 equality ipm: optimal warnings=["4 column(s) have more than 30% nonzeros; the normal equations will be dense (§8.3)"]' (same for the other three forms)

findings.title: IllConditionedTests' 'an answer this fragile must carry a warning' cannot fail for InteriorPoint()
findings.claim: Tests/ZTronLPIntegrationTests/IllConditionedTests.swift:99 '#expect(!analysis.warnings.isEmpty, "...: an answer this fragile must carry a warning")'; README §4 defect 9 'The answer carries a warning that the optimal basis is ill-conditioned'.
findings.observed: On these dense matrices (orders >= 4), InteriorPoint() always attaches the dense-column note, and so does Portfolio when the IPM answer wins. The assertion therefore holds whether or not an ill-conditioning or stall warning is produced. Nothing is hidden today: at orders 9 to 12, 0 of 144 solves carry only the dense-column note.
findings.whyWrong: The assertion is satisfied by a warning that has nothing to do with conditioning, so for the IPM it cannot catch a missing ill-conditioning warning, which is what it is there for.
findings.evidence: Every IPM answer from order 4 carries the dense-column warning; hilbertonly: 'order 10: 36 solves, far(>=1e-3) 36, any warning 36, only the dense-column warning 0' (identical at 11 and 12; order 9: far 30, any warning 36, only the dense-column warning 0)

findings.title: HANDBOOK and SPEC v0.2 say each layer imports only the layers beneath it; ZTronLPInteriorPoint imports ZTronLPSimplex
findings.claim: HANDBOOK.md:134 'Each layer imports only the layers beneath it; branch and bound and CP-SAT are the two that import an LP engine (§3)'; SPECIFICATION-v0.2.md:57 'The layering of v0.1 §3 stands: each layer imports only layers beneath it.'
findings.observed: Sources/ZTronLPInteriorPoint/InteriorPoint.swift:12 has 'import ZTronLPSimplex', and Package.swift declares the dependency. That is an LP engine importing another engine of the same layer (Package.swift 'MARK: Layer 3'). Package.swift:13-16 documents this edge itself; HANDBOOK and the SPEC deny it. Every other import matches Package.swift.
findings.whyWrong: Both documents state the layering as an invariant that the code does not satisfy.
findings.documented: Only in Package.swift comments ('Two edges deserve a note ... ZTronLPInteriorPoint imports ZTronLPSimplex'); HANDBOOK and SPEC state the opposite.

findings.title: Test mixedModelsAgreeAcrossStrategiesAndWorkerCounts runs one strategy
findings.claim: The test name (Tests/ZTronLPBranchAndBoundTests/BranchAndBoundTests.swift:187) promises agreement across strategies and across worker counts.
findings.observed: Over 8 random mixed models, the body runs only BranchAndBound(engine: Simplex(.dual)), at threads 1, 2 and 8. Each run is checked for status optimal and an integral, feasible point, and the runs are compared with each other to 1e-4 relative. There is no second strategy (no primal node engine, no CP-SAT, no Portfolio) and no reference optimum.
findings.whyWrong: A disagreement between node engines, or one shared wrong answer, on mixed models would not be caught. The name promises more than the assertions check.
findings.evidence: 'let analysis = try await BranchAndBound(engine: Simplex(.dual)).solve(lp, context: context)' inside 'for threads in [1, 2, 8]'; reference is the first run

findings.title: Package.swift declares Heap, OrderedCollections and BitCollections for ZTronLPCPSAT, which imports none of them
findings.claim: Package.swift:69-70 'Heap / OrderedDictionary / BitSet' as the reason for swift-collections; Package.swift:159 CPSAT dependencies 'atomics, heap, orderedCollections, bitCollections'.
findings.observed: No file of Sources/ZTronLPCPSAT imports HeapModule, OrderedCollections or BitCollections. OrderedDictionary, OrderedSet, BitSet and BitArray appear nowhere in Sources, and Heap is used only by ZTronLPBranchAndBound/SearchTree.swift.
findings.whyWrong: These are stale dependency declarations: every client compiles and links two collection modules it never uses, and the manifest's rationale is out of date.

findings.title: ci.yml's TSAN rule says threads = 8, but nothing sets it
findings.claim: .github/workflows/ci.yml:50 'Rule C10: Thread Sanitizer is clean on the integration suite with threads = 8.'
findings.observed: ZTronLPIntegrationTests never sets SolveContext.threads, and resolvedThreads defaults to ProcessInfo.activeProcessorCount (Strategy.swift:163-165). On a GitHub macos-latest arm64 runner (3 vCPUs) that means 3 workers; 8 holds only on an 8-core machine such as the baseline's.
findings.whyWrong: The stated configuration of the race check is not what the CI job runs.
findings.evidence: public var resolvedThreads: Int { Swift.max(1, threads ?? ProcessInfo.processInfo.activeProcessorCount) }

summary: Cycle B / F7 (oracles first). Every baseline gate passed. 546 tests ran in 13 targets, which matches README §5. I also ran the simplex, interior-point and facade test targets under TSAN, which neither CI nor the baseline covers: no reports. The deterministic published numbers I re-ran all match: netlib pivots, IPM and crossover counts, the transport LP, 20/20 B&B optima, CP-SAT 7/7 and 5/7, Metal candidates, and the Hilbert table except one column. The README §1 example prints exactly its comments. README §2 matches the public symbol graph: 117 top-level declarations, 22 nested types, every listed member and labelled signature present, every listed default equal. Independent KKT and certificate oracles confirm the duals, reduced costs and rays of the LP engines on the package's generator suite in both senses, which the integration tests never check. Findings: (B7-01, medium) 12 MIPLIB corpus cases return early and are reported as passed in every debug build, so CI's test job and its TSAN job never run the slow B&B and CP-SAT searches; (B7-02) the lint misses several spellings of C3 and C6 violations and never scans Tests/ (latent); (B7-03) the README Hilbert warning counts are wrong at orders 4 and 5; (B7-04) one IllConditioned assertion is satisfied by the IPM's unconditional dense-column warning; (B7-05) HANDBOOK and SPEC deny the InteriorPoint->Simplex import; (B7-06) a test name overpromises; (B7-07, B7-08, info) stale CP-SAT collection dependencies and an unenforced 'threads = 8' in ci.yml.
